question_text: An 18-year-old boy is brought to the emergency department by his parents because he suddenly collapsed while playing football. His parents mention that he had complained of dizziness while playing before, but never fainted in the middle of a game. On physical examination, the blood pressure is 130/90 mm Hg, the respirations are 15/min, and the pulse is 110/min. The chest is clear, but a systolic ejection murmur is present. The remainder of the examination revealed no significant findings. An electrocardiogram is ordered, along with an echocardiogram. He is diagnosed with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and the physician lists all the precautions he must follow. Which of the following drugs will be on the list of contraindicated substances?

                    ### Question
                    An 18-year-old boy is brought to the emergency department by his parents because he suddenly collapsed while playing football. His parents mention that he had complained of dizziness while playing before, but never fainted in the middle of a game. On physical examination, the blood pressure is 130/90 mm Hg, the respirations are 15/min, and the pulse is 110/min. The chest is clear, but a systolic ejection murmur is present. The remainder of the examination revealed no significant findings. An electrocardiogram is ordered, along with an echocardiogram. He is diagnosed with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and the physician lists all the precautions he must follow. Which of the following drugs will be on the list of contraindicated substances?

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
In hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), there is an increased risk of arrhythmias and impaired diastolic filling. Therefore, certain medications must be avoided. Dobutamine is a stimulant that can exacerbate arrhythmias, making it contraindicated in HCM. Nitrates can lead to hypotension, which is also a concern in HCM, thus they are contraindicated as well. Beta-blockers are beneficial in managing HCM by reducing heart rate and preventing arrhythmias, so they are not contraindicated. Potassium channel blockers have an unclear effect on HCM and may potentially cause arrhythmias, but their specific contraindication is not well established. Calcium channel blockers can worsen left ventricular outflow obstruction in HCM, making them contraindicated. Therefore, the most clearly contraindicated substances in this context are Dobutamine and Calcium channel blockers.
